title: Alcohol Use Disorder - Criteria
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: Criteria

CORE ALIASES: AUD, alcohol dependence, alcoholism, harmful alcohol use.

DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA: A problematic pattern of alcohol use leading to clinically significant impairment or distress, as manifested by at least two of the following, occurring within a 12-month period:
1. Alcohol taken in larger amounts or over longer period than intended
2. Persistent desire or unsuccessful efforts to cut down or control use
3. Great deal of time spent obtaining, using, or recovering
4. Craving or strong urge
5. Recurrent use resulting in failure to fulfill major role obligations
6. Continued use despite persistent social/interpersonal problems caused by alcohol
7. Important activities given up or reduced because of alcohol
8. Recurrent use in physically hazardous situations
9. Continued use despite knowledge of physical/psychological problem caused by alcohol
10. Tolerance
11. Withdrawal

Severity: Mild (2-3), Moderate (4-5), Severe (6+).

REQUIRED FEATURES: 2+ criteria in 12 months + clinically significant impairment/distress.

RULE-OUTS / DIFFERENTIALS: Other Substance Use Disorders, Bipolar (mood symptoms primary), Depressive disorders with self-medication, Medical conditions mimicking withdrawal.

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: "I only drink on weekends and never more than planned", "no cravings or withdrawal", "use has never caused problems at work or with family".

PROVENANCE: DSM-5-TR. NIAAA and APA guidelines support screening, brief intervention, and medications (naltrexone, acamprosate, disulfiram) + psychosocial treatment.
